hints.title: Arbitrary Path Highest Point
hints.text: The longest path between any two nodes in a tree might not pass through the root. How can you calculate the path length through every node as a potential highest point in a single traversal?

hints.title: Local Path Length Invariant
hints.text: The longest path passing through any specific node equals the depth of its left subtree plus the depth of its right subtree.

hints.title: Simultaneous Depth and Diameter Update
hints.text: Maintain a running maximum diameter initialized to 0. In a helper function, compute the depth of the left and right subtrees. Update the maximum diameter with left_depth + right_depth. Return 1 + max(left_depth, right_depth) to the parent caller.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (1 <= N <= 10^4)
H: tree height (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Every node is visited once, updating the global diameter at each node.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Calculating depth separately for every node in a top-down manner results in repeated visits, yielding O(N^2) time on degenerate trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bottom-up post-order traversal computes depth and updates the global diameter simultaneously in O(N) time and O(H) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Distinguishing between the value returned to the parent (height) and the value updating the global diameter (left_height + right_height), counting edges rather than nodes.

solutions.approach: Bottom-Up Height with Running Diameter Tracking
Bottom-Up Subtree Depth with Global Invariant
